title: Before You Sign a Roofing Contract
description: Before you sign a Houston roofing contract, get the permit, the underlayment, and the per-sheet deck price in writing. A monthly payment is not a scope.
html:
A roofing contract is a scope with a price on it, not a handshake and a color. The bids that cause trouble are vague in the same places: permit, underlayment, decking, and who actually stands on the roof. Ask those before you sign. A straight contractor already has the answers.

The lines worth reading twice

  • Who pulls the permit, for which city, and is it in the price.
  • The underlayment by type, not the word “synthetic” with no product behind it.
  • Decking by the sheet, so a soft spot is not a new argument.
  • Flashing: pipe boots, valleys, walls, and chimney, named, not “as needed.”
  • Who registers the manufacturer warranty, and what a lifetime shingle warranty does not cover.
  • A payment schedule that is not the full price before the tear-off.
  • Proof of insurance for the crew on your roof, not a logo on a yard sign.

If the only difference you can see is the monthly payment, you are comparing financing, not roofs. Financing is useful. It is not the product. Our financing page is there when the cash is the problem. The scope still has to say what is being built.

What we put on paper

You should be able to hand our scope to another roofer and have them price the same work. Brand, color, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, dumpster, magnet sweep, and the permit. If a storm is involved, the contract does not assign us your entire claim. You stay the one who talks to the carrier. We meet the adjuster and write what we see.

Read it at the table, not on the tailgate. If a line is missing, ask for it in the document, not in a text you will lose. When you want that conversation with us, request a free inspection or call (281) 541-0027.
